anf_compare.notes: ANF/NPNF has no text of this letter; translated directly from the PG 77 Greek.

choices.english: …and that he has been thrown out unlawfully
choices.why: The infinitive is still governed by φησι in the previous section: Peter's reported complaint. ἀθέσμως is 'unlawfully'.
προσεπάγω is 'add further'; the subject is still Peter.

choices.term: στη 279 σάτω τοῦ πρεσβύτου τὸ δάκρυον
rejected: shed a tear for the presbyter at the 279th
choices.why: στησάτω (aorist imperative of ἵστημι) is split by the PG column number 279; the number is not text.

choices.english: bearing in mind … and yielding besides to our letters
rejected: Your holiness should consider that this appears to be in accordance with divine canons
choices.why: Both are participles agreeing with ἡ σὴ ὁσιότης and lead to the imperative στησάτω; they are not separate statements.

choices.english: he chooses / let him be tried / he objects
choices.why: The subject is Peter. Only αὐτῆς is feminine, and it refers to θεοσέβεια ('your piety').

choices.term: τῶν ὑπὸ τὴν αὐτῆς χεῖρα θεοσεβεστάτων ἐπισκόπων
choices.english: the most God-fearing bishops under your authority
rejected: the godly bishops under her hand
choices.why: αὐτῆς refers back to τῆς σῆς θεοσεβείας, so the bishops are under Domnus; 'your' makes this plain in English.

choices.term: τὴν ἐσομένην ἐπ' αὐτῷ κρίσιν παραλύουσα, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐν
choices.english: that undoes the judgment he will receive, by making it seem not to have been…
rejected: the impending judgment upon him being dissolved, so that not in money or possessions
choices.why: The clause runs on into the next section (δίκῃ πεποιῆσθαι δοκεῖν); the Greek says nothing about money here.

lemmas.gloss: to move by entreaty; passive 'be moved, yield' (aorist passive participle)
middle/passive: to go to law, be tried (present imperative)

pass_a_gloss: [Continuing Peter's reported speech:] and to have been thrown out (ἐκβάλλω, pf. pass. inf.) lawlessly (ἀθέσμως), adding further (προσεπάγω, pres. ptc.) that also all the money (χρήματα) belonging (προσήκω, ptc.) to him was snatched (ἁρπάζω, aor. pass.). Your holiness (ὁσιότης), therefore (τοιγαροῦν), bearing in mind (ἐννοέω, pres. ptc. fem.) both what seems good (δοκέω, ptc.) to the divine canons (κανών) and what is fitting (πρέπω, ptc.) to a church and to those appointed (τάσσω, pf. pass. ptc.) to sacred ministry (λειτουργία), and still besides these, having been moved/put to shame (δυσωπέω, aor. pass. ptc. fem.) by the letters (γράμματα) from us, let it stop (ἵστημι, aor. impv. 3 sg., στησάτω; split by column number 279) the tear (δάκρυον) of the old man (πρεσβύτης). And if he should choose (αἱρέομαι, aor. opt.) to go to law (δικάζω, aor. mid. inf.) against those bringing (ἐπάγω, ptc.) the charges (αἰτία) against him, let him be tried (δικάζω, pres. mid./pass. impv.) according to what is customary (εἰωθός) before your God-fearingness (θεοσέβεια), being present together (συμπάρειμι, ptc., gen. abs.), clearly (δηλονότι), the most God-fearing (θεοσεβέστατος) bishops (ἐπίσκοπος) under her [= your God-fearingness's] hand (χείρ), except if he should decline (παραιτέομαι, pres. opt.) some as suspect (ὕποπτος). For we believe (πιστεύω) that none of the most God-fearing bishops thinks (φρονέω) hostile things (ἐχθρός) toward a brother (ἀδελφός); but in order that this may not become a pretext (πρόφασις), loosening/undoing (παραλύω, pres. ptc. fem.) the judgment (κρίσις) that will be (εἰμί, fut. ptc.) upon him, toward its not in [continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: …and that he has been thrown out unlawfully; and he adds that all the money belonging to him was seized as well.

Let your holiness, then, bearing in mind what the divine canons decree and what befits the church and those appointed to sacred ministry, and yielding besides to our letters, stop the old man's tears. And if he chooses to go to trial against those who bring the charges against him, let him be tried in the customary way before your piety, with the most God-fearing bishops under your authority sitting with you, of course, unless he objects to some of them as suspect. For we do not believe that any of the most God-fearing bishops harbors hostility toward a brother; but so that this may not become a pretext that undoes the judgment he will receive, by making it seem not to have been…
source_text:
καὶ ἀθέσμως ἐκβεβλῆσθαι, προσεπάγων ὅτι καὶ ἡρπάσθη πάντα τὰ προσήκοντα αὐτῷ
χρήματα.
Ἡ σὴ τοιγαροῦν ὁσιότης ἐννοοῦσα καὶ τὸ τοῖς θείοις κανόσι δοκοῦν καὶ τὸ
πρέπον ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ τοῖς τεταγμένοις εἰς ἱερὰν λειτουργίαν, ἔτι τε πρὸς τούτοις καὶ
τὰ παρ' ἡμῶν δυσωπηθεῖσα γράμματα, στη 279 σάτω τοῦ πρεσβύτου τὸ δάκρυον. Καὶ
εἰ μὲν ἕλοιτο δικάσασθαι πρὸς τοὺς ἐπάγοντας αὐτῷ τὰς αἰτίας, δικαζέσθω κατὰ τὸ
εἰωθὸς ἐπὶ τῆς σῆς θεοσεβείας, συμπαρόντων δηλονότι τῶν ὑπὸ τὴν αὐτῆς χεῖρα
θεοσεβεστάτων ἐπισκόπων, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ παραιτοῖτό τινας ὡς ὑπόπτους· οὐδένα μὲν
γὰρ τῶν θεοσεβεστάτων ἐπισκόπων ἐχθρὰ φρονεῖν ἀδελφῷ πιστεύομεν, ἵνα δὲ μὴ
πρόφασις αὕτη γένηται, τὴν ἐσομένην ἐπ' αὐτῷ κρίσιν παραλύουσα, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐν
source_normalizations: 'στη 279 σάτω' is στησάτω split by the PG column number 279; the number is not text and is not translated.
reviewer: claude source review, separate pass (same model family as the drafter)
notes: The section opens inside Peter's reported speech (φησι in the previous section governs ἐκβεβλῆσθαι).
The section ends mid-sentence at πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐν; the next section supplies δίκῃ πεποιῆσθαι δοκεῖν and opens '…justly done'.
The earlier draft listed 1 Timothy 3:1-3 as allusions; none fits the passage (ἱερὰν λειτουργίαν, θεοσέβεια and ἐχθρὰ φρονεῖν are ordinary church vocabulary), so no Scripture is cited.

review.coverage: every clause checked against the source
changes: Opening clause restored as Peter's reported complaint ('…and that he has been thrown out unlawfully; and he adds that …').
στη|σάτω read as the imperative 'stop the old man's tears'; column number 279 removed from the sense.
Subject of ἕλοιτο / δικαζέσθω / παραιτοῖτο corrected from 'she' to 'he' (Peter); the bishops are under Domnus's authority.
Garbled last clause replaced; it now runs into the next section ('…by making it seem not to have been…').
Paragraphs follow the two source paragraphs; three unfounded 1 Timothy 3 references removed.
Justification rebuilt 2026-10-24 to match the corrected English; old machine-draft glosses and choices replaced.
checked: agency: Peter is the subject of the trial verbs; αὐτῆς = your piety
modality: imperatives στησάτω and δικαζέσθω; optatives ἕλοιτο and παραιτοῖτο in the conditions
negation: οὐδένα … ἐχθρὰ φρονεῖν πιστεύομεν; ἵνα δὲ μὴ
